subject: Biology
title: Locomotion Physiology Master Glossary & High-Yield NEST Traps
learningObjectives: Master 10 high-frequency NEST traps and deceptive questions in locomotion physiology
Review 35+ core anatomical, biochemical, and clinical definitions
Reinforce sarcomere dimensional invariants and skeletal formulas
content:
### High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps Table

| Misconception / Trap | Biological Reality | Exam Tip / Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *"The length of the A-band shortens during muscle contraction."* | The **A-band length remains CONSTANT**. Only the I-band and H-zone shorten/disappear. | A-band reflects the fixed physical length of thick myosin filaments. |
| *"Calcium binds to Tropomyosin during muscle contraction."* | $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ binds specifically to **Troponin-C (TnC)**, causing a conformational shift in Tropomyosin. | Troponin-C has 4 $\text{Ca}^{2+}$-binding sites. |
| *"Rigor mortis occurs because muscle cells are flooded with excess ATP."* | Rigor mortis occurs due to **ATP DEPLETION**; fresh ATP is required to break cross-bridges. | Without ATP, myosin heads remain permanently bound to actin. |
| *"Gout is caused by deposition of calcium oxalate crystals in joints."* | Gout is caused by deposition of **Monosodium Urate Crystals** (from uric acid purine breakdown). | Calcium oxalate forms renal calculi (kidney stones). |
| *"Myasthenia Gravis is a genetic dystrophin deficiency."* | Myasthenia Gravis is an **Autoimmune disease targeting ACh receptors**. Dystrophin deficiency causes **Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy**. | Do not confuse MG (autoimmune) with DMD (genetic). |
| *"The human adult skull has 22 bones and articulates with 1 occipital condyle."* | The human skull is **Dicondylic** (possesses **2 Occipital Condyles** articulating with Atlas). | Monocondylic skulls are found in Reptiles and Birds. |
| *"False ribs do not articulate with the vertebral column."* | False ribs (8th, 9th, 10th) articulate dorsally with vertebrae; they join the **7th costal cartilage** ventrally. | **Floating ribs (11th & 12th)** remain unattached ventrally. |
| *"Red muscle fibers fatigue rapidly because they perform anaerobic glycolysis."* | Red fibers are **Slow-Twitch, Aerobic, rich in Myoglobin/Mitochondria, and FATIGUE-RESISTANT**. | White muscle fibers perform anaerobic glycolysis and fatigue rapidly. |
| *"Tetany is caused by hypercalcemia (excess calcium)."* | Tetany is caused by **HYPOCALCEMIA (low serum $\text{Ca}^{2+}$)**, causing neuronal membrane hyper-excitability. | Hypercalcemia depresses nervous system excitability. |
| *"The joint between Atlas and Axis is a hinge joint."* | The Atlanto-axial joint ($\text{C}_1\text{--}\text{C}_2$) is a **PIVOT JOINT** allowing rotational "No" movement. | The Atlanto-occipital joint is a condyloid joint ("Yes" motion). |

---

### Master Glossary for Locomotion Physiology

- **A-Band (Anisotropic Band)**: Dark central region of a sarcomere extending the fixed physical length of thick myosin filaments.
- **Acetabulum**: Deep lateral cup-shaped socket on the pelvic coxal bone articulating with the head of the Femur.
- **Actin**: Primary contractile protein of thin myofilaments (globular G-actin polymerizing into filamentous F-actin).
- **Acromion Process**: Lateral terminal expansion of the scapular spine articulating with the clavicle.
- **Amphiarthrosis**: Slightly movable cartilaginous joint (e.g., Pubic symphysis, intervertebral discs).
- **Atlas ($\text{C}_1$)**: First cervical vertebra articulating with dicondylic skull to allow "Yes" nodding motion.
- **Axis ($\text{C}_2$)**: Second cervical vertebra featuring an odontoid process allowing "No" rotational motion.
- **Cartilaginous Joint**: Joint connected entirely by hyaline or fibrocartilage lacking a synovial cavity.
- **Clavicle**: Collar bone; S-shaped bone forming the anterior pectoral girdle.
- **Creatine Phosphate**: High-energy phosphate buffer compound for rapid ATP regeneration in muscle.
- **Cross-Bridge**: Temporary physical linkage formed when high-energy myosin head binds actin.
- **Diarthrosis (Synovial Joint)**: Freely movable joint characterized by a fluid-filled synovial cavity.
- **Dystrophin**: Structural protein anchoring actin myofilaments to the sarcolemma, absent in DMD.
- **Endomysium**: Delicate connective tissue sheath surrounding an individual muscle fiber.
- **Fascia**: Dense sheath of collagenous connective tissue binding multiple muscle fascicles together.
- **Fascicle**: Discrete bundle of skeletal muscle fibers within a muscle.
- **Femur**: Thigh bone; longest, heaviest, and strongest bone in the human skeleton.
- **Glenoid Cavity**: Shallow lateral depression on the scapula articulating with head of Humerus.
- **Gout**: Metabolic disorder characterized by monosodium urate crystal deposition in synovial joints.
- **H-Zone**: Central lighter zone of an A-band containing thick myosin filaments exclusively.
- **I-Band (Isotropic Band)**: Light band of a sarcomere containing thin actin filaments exclusively.
- **Intercalated Disc**: Specialized intercellular junction in cardiac muscle containing desmosomes and gap junctions.
- **Light Meromyosin (LMM)**: Fibrous tail component of a meromyosin molecule.
- **M-Line**: Fine proteinaceous membrane bisecting the H-zone that links adjacent thick filaments.
- **Myasthenia Gravis**: Autoimmune neuromuscular disorder with antibodies blocking Nicotinic ACh receptors.
- **Myofibril**: Cylindrical contractile organelle within a muscle fiber composed of repeating sarcomeres.
- **Myoglobin**: Iron- and oxygen-binding hemeprotein present in high concentrations in red muscle fibers.
- **Myosin**: Motor protein component of thick muscle myofilaments possessing intrinsic ATPase activity.
- **Osteoarthritis**: Degenerative "wear-and-tear" joint disease marked by erosion of articular hyaline cartilage.
- **Osteoporosis**: Age-related reduction in bone mineral density leading to porous, fragile bones.
- **Patella**: Knee cap; triangular sesamoid bone formed within the quadriceps tendon.
- **Pectoral Girdle**: Shoulder girdle comprising 2 Clavicles and 2 Scapulae (4 bones).
- **Pelvic Girdle**: Hip girdle comprising 2 Coxal bones formed by fusion of Ilium, Ischium, and Pubis.
- **Perimysium**: Connective tissue sheath surrounding a muscle fascicle.
- **Power Stroke**: Pivoting motion of the myosin head that pulls actin filaments inward toward the M-line.
- **Red Muscle Fibers**: Slow-twitch, aerobic muscle fibers rich in myoglobin, mitochondria, and capillaries.
- **Rheumatoid Arthritis**: Autoimmune joint disease producing Rheumatoid Factor (IgM) leading to pannus formation.
- **Rigor Mortis**: Post-mortem muscle stiffness caused by ATP depletion preventing cross-bridge detachment.
- **Sarcolemma**: Plasma membrane surrounding a skeletal muscle fiber.
- **Sarcomere**: Functional contractile unit of a myofibril bounded by two adjacent Z-discs.
- **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum**: Specialized smooth ER of muscle cells that stores and releases $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions.
- **Sesamoid Bone**: Bone formed by ossification within a tendon (e.g., Patella).
- **Sliding Filament Theory**: Mechanism of muscle contraction where thin actin filaments slide over thick myosin filaments.
- **Synarthrosis**: Immovable fibrous joint (e.g., Sutures of the skull).
- **T-Tubule**: Invaginations of the sarcolemma conducting action potentials deep into muscle fibers.
- **Tetany**: Involuntary muscular spasms caused by hypocalcemia (low serum $\text{Ca}^{2+}$).
- **Troponin**: Heterotrimeric regulatory protein complex (TnT, TnI, TnC) bound to tropomyosin on thin filaments.
- **Tropomyosin**: Fibrous protein winding along actin grooves that masks myosin-binding sites during rest.
- **White Muscle Fibers**: Fast-twitch, anaerobic muscle fibers low in myoglobin, specialized for rapid powerful bursts.
- **Z-Disc (Z-Line)**: Dense protein membrane bisecting the I-band that anchors thin actin filaments.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Essential Formulas & Numerical Invariants
conceptBreakdown.explanation:
1. Human Skeleton = 206 Bones (Axial: 80, Appendicular: 126).
2. Skull Associated = 29 Bones (Cranial: 8, Facial: 14, Hyoid: 1, Auditory: 6).
3. Vertebral Formula = C7 T12 L5 S1 Co1 = 26 Vertebrae.
4. Ribs = 12 Pairs (24 Bones: True 1–7, False 8–10, Floating 11–12).
5. Phalangeal Formula = 2.3.3.3.3 = 14 Phalanges per hand/foot.
